findings.claim: The claude engine's allow-listed child environment drops C3_CHILD, so a reviewer/worker on the claude engine does not see C3_CHILD=1 and the hook repair is not suppressed there.

child_environment() builds the env from the allow-list plus DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER and endpoint vars only; C3_CHILD set by scrub_host_markers never passes through.
scrub_host_markers() sets C3_CHILD=1 on generic subprocess children, and hook_line() relies on in_c3_child() to stay read-only inside reviewers/workers.

findings.claim: c3 branches --set/--clear interpolates the branch name into a git config key, so names with dots or unusual characters can address the wrong subsection or fail; a foreign note starting with 'c3: ' is misclassified as C3's record.

evidence.observation: set_state/clear_state build key branch.{branch}.description by string interpolation and pass it to git config; parse_descriptions strips branch./.description symmetrically, which breaks down for dotted/odd names.
is_c3_description is a plain starts_with('c3: ') on the first line, so a user's note beginning with 'c3: ' is treated as a record and --set discards its first line.

findings.verification: Try --set/--clear on dotted and odd branch names and on a foreign note starting with 'c3: ', then inspect git config and the preserved text.
findings.remedy: Quote/escape the config subsection (or use git config --fixed-value / branch.<name> via lower-level ref handling with validation), refuse or delimit ambiguous names, and require a full record parse before treating a first line as C3's.

findings.claim: The c3 branches listing and c3 doctor, both described as read-only, run git status --porcelain in the primary worktree. Git refreshes the index and can create index.lock unless optional locks are disabled. The hook and c3 finish do not run status.

The invariant requires nothing outside the worktree to be removed on any error path.
findings.trigger: A reviewer leaves a junction inside the throwaway worktree (for example node_modules pointing at the main checkout) and unlink fails or does not see it.

evidence.observation: unlink_links_inside's result is discarded. git worktree remove --force and remove_dir_all always follow.
Only FileType::is_symlink is unlinked. Other directory entries are pushed on the walk stack.
The Windows test asserts a successful unlink of one junction. It does not run remove() after a failed unlink.
This review did not establish whether Git follows a junction that is still present.

findings.verification: On Windows, hold a junction open so remove_dir fails, call the remove path, and check that a sentinel outside the worktree still exists.
findings.remedy: If unlink_links_inside did not remove every reparse point (use the same FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT test as panel/roles.rs), skip git worktree remove and remove_dir_all and leave the directory for a later prune. Do not delete when any link remains.

history.note: wave P4 (telemetry, kimi worktree removal), commit 08ae5d5

reviewer_checks.note: Out of this range (fixes: none); untouched by this patch.
The Kimi removal implementation in this range still proceeds after ignored unlink errors.

findings.claim: Not every process C3 starts gets C3_CHILD=1. The claude auth-status and --version probe clears the environment and does not set it. The detached maintain process is CreateProcessW with a null environment block, so it only inherits a parent that already has the variable.
findings.trigger: A launcher probe or a maintain pass spawned from a user session that does not already have C3_CHILD.

evidence.observation: probe() calls env_clear and then only the probe env pairs. scrub_host_markers is not called. Callers pass auth status and --version.
CreateProcessW is called with lpEnvironment null. The command line is the maintain --run pass, not a Claude session.
Reviewer and worker turns do call scrub_host_markers after env_clear, so those CLIs get C3_CHILD=1.

findings.verification: Log the environment of claude auth status as started by sign_in, and of the detached maintain pid, and check for C3_CHILD.
findings.remedy: Set C3_CHILD=1 on the probe command and in the detached maintain environment block. Document that Claude subagents must inherit it.

reviewer_checks.note: Out of this range (fixes: none); untouched by this patch.
The Claude probe and detached Windows maintenance paths still bypass the normal marker injection.

findings.claim: Branch classification is wrong in two ordinary layouts. If origin/HEAD is unset and both main and develop exist, main is the default even when the repo's real default is develop, so merged and unknown are computed against the wrong branch. A worktree whose directory name starts with c3-kimi-wt- is dropped from the leftover count even when it is the user's.
findings.trigger: A repository with no origin/HEAD, a local main, and develop as the real default; or a worktree directory named c3-kimi-wt-notes.

evidence.observation: default_branch uses origin/HEAD when that local branch exists, otherwise the first of main and master that exists, otherwise the current branch.
is_c3_throwaway_worktree is true when the path's file name starts with c3-kimi-wt-. The scan skips those worktrees.

findings.verification: In a repo with branches main and develop, no origin/HEAD, and develop checked out, run c3 branches and read default_branch. Add a worktree whose folder name starts with c3-kimi-wt- and confirm it is absent.
findings.remedy: Prefer init.defaultBranch and the branch HEAD is born from over a hard-coded main. Treat a worktree as throwaway only when its path is under the temp directory and the name matches the prefix plus the uuid pattern.

reviewer_checks.note: Out of this range (fixes: none); untouched by this patch.
The scanner still prefers local `main` over a custom default and ignores worktrees by basename prefix.

findings.claim: Two privacy and fetch bounds are wider than the stated invariants. For vendor class anthropic, any id of the shape claude-(fable|opus|sonnet|haiku)-<digits>[-<digits>] is sent by name even when it is not in the closed list or the published set. Catalog reads stop at HTTP_BODY_CAP (8 MiB), not the 4 MiB BODY_CAP, and the redirect allow-list permits code.kimi.ai to cdn.kimi.ai for every keyless GET, not only the installer.
findings.trigger: A reviewer classified as anthropic (engine claude with no private base_url, or a host under anthropic.com) whose model is a custom id of that shape; or a catalog that redirects or sends a 5 to 8 MiB body.

evidence.observation: After the closed list misses, class anthropic returns the lowercased id when is_published_claude_shape matches. published_ids is not consulted.
HTTP_BODY_CAP is 8 * 1024 * 1024. read_capped uses that cap. web.rs BODY_CAP is 4 MiB and is applied only after a successful read.
redirect_target allows REDIRECT_HOSTS (code.kimi.ai, cdn.kimi.ai) for every follow_redirects GET, including web::keyless_get.

findings.verification: Emit a telemetry model token for engine claude and model claude-opus-9-9 with an empty published set. Fetch a catalog through a 302 from code.kimi.ai to cdn.kimi.ai and confirm it is followed.
findings.remedy: Send a Claude-shaped id only when it is in CLAUDE_MODELS or the published set. Cap the keyless read at BODY_CAP inside http_get when the caller is the catalog fetch. Restrict the kimi CDN pair to the installer URLs.

history.note: fetch part: wave P3, commit 8e6fd3e; Claude-shape part: wave P4, commit 08ae5d5

reviewer_checks.note: Out of this range (fixes: none); untouched by this patch.
The telemetry shape exception, shared redirect exception, and 8 MiB transport cap all remain.

findings.claim: --clear deletes the first line of any description that starts with c3: , including a human note that does not parse as a record. --set, if git config --get fails, treats the description as empty and overwrites it, dropping a foreign note it could not read.
findings.trigger: A branch description whose first line is c3: hello, or a git config --get that exits non-zero while a description is present.

evidence.observation: is_c3_description is starts_with("c3: "). clear_state removes that first line whenever this is true, without BranchRecord::parse.
read_description(...).unwrap_or_default() turns a failed read into an empty string, then git config writes the new record over the key.

findings.verification: Set a description to c3: not a record\nkeep me and run c3 branches --clear. Separately, make git config --get fail and run --set; check whether the previous value remains.
findings.remedy: Treat a c3: line as C3's only when BranchRecord::parse succeeds; otherwise leave it. If the read fails, abort --set instead of writing.

reviewer_checks.note: Out of this range (fixes: none); untouched by this patch.
Any `c3: ` prefix still counts as a record, and `--set` still treats a failed description read as empty.

findings.claim: The agy step classifier misses real writes whose parameter keys lack the nine marker fragments: only top-level keys are tested, nested objects are ignored, and a command carried in a value (or a writer with fixed-path parameters such as action/destination/text) is judged a reader, so a real write with a tree change becomes a 'reply kept' warning instead of a failure.
findings.trigger: An agy tool step with parameters like {"action": "rm -rf x"}, {"config": {"path": "a.rs"}}, or a fixed-target writer taking only text/content.

evidence.observation: agy_tool_step_is_writing returns non-writing when parameters are an object with no top-level key containing a marker; markers are only path/file/dir/folder/cwd/command/cmd/target/uri and only obj.keys() are tested.
engine_tree_outcome fails only on non-empty agy.writing; otherwise a complete reply warns, so a missed write directly flips fail to warned.

findings.verification: Unit-test agy_tool_step_is_writing with nested-path params and a command-in-value step and assert both count as writing.
findings.remedy: Also inspect nested parameter objects and well-known value shapes, or treat unknown tool names with object parameters as writing unless the name is an allow-listed reader; add fixtures with nested-path and value-embedded-command steps.

findings.claim: The ACTIVE/DONE merge keeps the first logged parameters object per (index, name) and an unnamed or parameter-less ACTIVE step counts as writing, so a read-only step whose DONE event carries the parameters (or a renamed/re-indexed continuation) fails a run that actually only read, discarding a complete reply.
findings.trigger: Agy logs a read_file ACTIVE event without tool_info.parameters and the DONE event with them, or logs the same logical step under a different name or without step_index.

evidence.observation: Steps merge only on matching index and name and keep the first parameters seen; a step whose parameters were not logged is writing, and an unnamed step is kept with an empty name that the classifier counts as writing.
Writing steps are collected from merged steps and any non-empty writing list fails the run even when the monitored compare is clean.

findings.verification: Feed a two-event read step (parameter-less ACTIVE, parameterized DONE) to read_agy_events and assert writing_tool_names stays empty.
findings.remedy: Merge parameters across all events of a step (prefer any object seen, not the first), and treat a parameter-less ACTIVE event as unknown only until its DONE/ERROR event is seen.

findings.claim: A brief committed at HEAD but unreadable in the live tree passes the preflight yet fails later at staging as a capability ProviderFailure, which the panel does not re-seat; meanwhile the isolation paragraph unconditionally claims the brief was copied whenever the ref is stageable.
findings.trigger: Brief committed at HEAD whose live file is deleted, locked, or unreadable; or staging fails (read-only worktree parent, disk error) while the prompt still says it was copied in.

evidence.observation: isolated_brief_refusal returns None when cat-file HEAD:ref succeeds even if the live source cannot be opened, so the seat launches.

Staging copies the live brief.src and on error returns a capability ProviderFailure, not a preflight refusal; the prompt line appends the copied-in sentence for every stageable ref without checking staging.

findings.verification: Delete the live brief while it stays committed at HEAD, launch a kimi seat, and check whether the panel re-seats it and what the prompt claims.
findings.remedy: Refuse at preflight only when the seat can actually proceed (fall back to materializing the brief from HEAD), or make the staging failure a preflight-class refusal; gate the copied-in sentence on staging success.

findings.claim: The pre-panel snapshot narrows finding ids but still reads every finding's live status, so a sibling that changes a shown finding's status mid-panel changes the member's verdict; concurrent findings-store writes from two members or two c3 processes can also last-writer-win.
findings.trigger: A sibling transitions F02-1 proposed->fixed while a member judged against the pre-panel snapshot is still running, or two members commit findings concurrently.

evidence.observation: run_open_priors filters by listed ids but takes status from the store as it stands (fresh status), per its own doc comment.
No locking or merge of the findings store is introduced by this patch; the snapshot is an id list, not a status/version snapshot.

findings.verification: Flip a listed finding's status mid-panel in a fixture and assert the running member's prior-blocker disposition still uses the shown status.
findings.remedy: Snapshot (id, status) pairs per member at panel start and judge against those; serialize findings-store updates with file locking or read-modify-write retries.

findings.claim: The smoke can pass while a sub-agent surface exists: tools under any mcp__ namespace are exempt even when named exactly like multi-agent tools, an opted-in seat passes without exercising the switch, and a future CLI using a new namespace or new session_meta field names yields 'unproven' failure on sound updates but any new tool name inside the collaboration namespace is the only future-proofed case.
findings.trigger: A CLI serving spawn_agent through an mcp__ namespace, or a smoke roster whose codex entries all set codex_config to allow sub-agents.

evidence.observation: is_multi_agent_tool returns false for any namespace starting with mcp__, so collaboration tools wrapped as MCP are neither offered nor called.
Consults with subagents_allowed true are skipped, and all-opted-in yields Pass with only a stderr note.

findings.verification: Craft a rollout offering collaboration.spawn_agent under namespace mcp__srv and assert subagent_switch_check fails.
findings.remedy: Count exact multi-agent tool names regardless of namespace, fail (not pass) when every consult opted in, and pin the tested CLI version's rollout shape in the failure message.

findings.claim: Every codex review turn now unconditionally passes two new -c keys on the claim that an older CLI ignores unknown keys, with no version gate or fallback; if any supported older CLI rejects unknown -c keys, all codex reviews fail.
findings.trigger: Run a codex review turn on an older codex-cli that errors on unknown -c keys.

evidence.observation: bridge_config_for appends REVIEW_ISOLATION for every codex review turn minus only user-named keys; no CLI-version check exists.
The ignorability claim for older CLIs lives only in a comment on REVIEW_ISOLATION; no test exercises an older CLI.

findings.verification: Run bridge_config_for against the oldest supported codex-cli and confirm the turn starts.
findings.remedy: Probe the CLI's supported keys once per version (or retry a rejected turn without the new keys) and document the oldest CLI actually tested.

findings.claim: The death-record fallback covers only single detached runs: panel members never note their stream, and a reader of a dead run passes noted: None, so a panel member that dies in a read-insist re-ask still gets empty events_file/last_event/events_mtime/partial_hint.
findings.trigger: A detached panel whose member dies in its read-insist re-ask after the commit removed the pending record.

evidence.observation: note_engine_stream is called only when detach is active and panel_member is none; the reader path passes noted: None.

findings.verification: Kill a panel member in its read-insist turn and inspect the reader-written death record's events fields.
findings.remedy: Note the stream for panel members as well (keyed by member) or have the reader fall back to the newest matching events file for the dead turn.

findings.claim: Agy can record a genuine write as a usable warning, while unfamiliar readers can be classified as writers and lose a complete review.
findings.trigger: A write step logs an empty object before the populated update, nests its command under an unrecognized key, shares an index with a finish event, or is omitted from the tool log. A read-only tool outside the allowlist can fail when its argument is named `path`.

evidence.observation: The parser keeps the first object, the handover exemption uses the index alone, and the classifier examines only top-level parameter names.
The fake engine writes inside its own launcher without a tool event. The test expects success, and the warning asserts the change was someone else's.

findings.verification: Add a fake write step with an empty ACTIVE object and a populated DONE command, then verify the unchanged classifier reports the run as usable.
findings.remedy: Classify recognized tools by capability and use the full step evidence. Restrict the handover exemption to a verified finish call and describe unexplained changes as unattributed.

findings.claim: Agy can commit a schema-valid verdict as usable after the bound brief or an artifact changed while it was reading.
findings.trigger: An editor or another process changes a bound input during the run, and agy returns a structured answer with no detected write.

evidence.observation: Bound-input drift is fed into the same warning branch as ambient drift. Completeness is derived from the outcome and the parsed structure.

findings.verification: Have fake agy wait while a second process replaces a bound artifact, then return a valid verdict and inspect the ledger outcome.
findings.remedy: Bind the review to immutable input bytes or classify bound-input drift separately and withhold the verdict until a consistent input was reviewed.

findings.claim: The Kimi staging path can overwrite a file outside the throwaway worktree before the reviewer starts.
findings.trigger: HEAD checks out a symlink at the brief destination, or a linked ancestor, and the live checkout supplies a readable regular brief at the corresponding lexical path.

evidence.observation: The brief reference is derived lexically. The destination is joined and passed to `create_dir_all` and `fs::copy` without rejecting linked components.
A platform that checks out the symlink and follows it when opening the copy destination can truncate the link target.

findings.verification: Use RC1 on a symlink-capable filesystem.
findings.remedy: Stage into a bridge-owned directory with a new file, or open the destination beneath an anchored worktree directory while rejecting links and reparse points at every component.

findings.claim: Kimi's availability check can reject a reachable brief or admit one that later fails staging without a reserve re-seat.
findings.trigger: The operator uses an in-repo path containing `..`, the HEAD destination conflicts with the live layout, or the live source becomes unreadable between validation and copy.

evidence.observation: The check uses a lexical path, opens only the source, and uses `cat-file -e` without establishing a regular staged file. A copy failure is returned as a provider capability failure.
Re-seat requires a reserved optional slot and recognized refusal wording.

findings.verification: In a disposable panel, test an in-repo `sub/../brief.md`, then test a readable live brief whose HEAD destination is a directory. Check whether the launcher starts or a reserve is drawn.
findings.remedy: Resolve a contained source and stage the exact bytes before committing the seat to launch. Route safe staging failures through a typed pre-start refusal.

findings.claim: The Kimi prompt discloses live-only names from across the checkout, including names outside the requested review and filenames with embedded line breaks.
findings.trigger: A tracked change or untracked file has a sensitive name and sorts into the first twenty status entries, or a filename contains Markdown delimiters or newlines.

evidence.observation: Repository-wide status includes untracked paths. Paths are interpolated verbatim between backticks and included in the outbound review prompt.

findings.verification: Capture the fake Kimi prompt with a synthetic confidential untracked filename outside the reviewed path.
findings.remedy: Default to a count or an explicitly scoped path list. Encode displayed paths as data before inserting them into the prompt.

findings.claim: Panel acceptance is not evaluated against the blocker records each member was shown.
findings.trigger: A listed finding changes status or severity between prompt creation and finish, or a member reports a sibling's newly created ID after that sibling commits.

evidence.observation: Only IDs are frozen. Subsequent reads supply the current status, severity, text, and existence check. The ledger and reviewer-check delta accept a prior report before the filtered semantics are applied.
The commit lock serializes merges against the current disk store. It does not freeze what reviewers saw.

findings.verification: Use RC3 and repeat with a prior report naming a newly committed sibling finding.
findings.remedy: Carry immutable prompt records in the member spec and use them for prompt rendering, semantics, and prior-report validation. Merge allowed checks separately into the current store.

findings.claim: Automatic maintenance can treat an unexercised Codex sub-agent switch as a passing smoke and skip rollback.
findings.trigger: The available smoke seat opts into sub-agents, or one successful consult leaves no thread ID while the other leaves a clean rollout.

evidence.observation: Two subprocess successes are required, but blank thread IDs are skipped and all opted-in threads explicitly return `Pass`. The update attempts rollback only for `Fail`.

findings.verification: Run the real smoke entry points with one clean thread and one successful blank-thread result, then repeat on an opted-in seat and inspect the update result.
findings.remedy: Require provenance for each expected turn and at least one designated guard-off smoke seat. Represent unexercised evidence as a hold or failure for automatic updates.

findings.claim: The rollout parser can treat incomplete or unrelated evidence as proof, and the parent smoke can fail to locate a sound child rollout under a relative home.
findings.trigger: The selected file has a clean prefix with an incomplete later record, an `additional_tools` event with a non-array or moved `tools` field, a mismatched metadata ID, or a relative `CODEX_HOME` interpreted from the smoke repository.

evidence.observation: Lookup selects by filename and mtime. Reading snapshots the length, skips malformed lines, and increments evidence for `additional_tools` before validating the tools array. No terminal event or session ID is checked.
The consult subprocess runs from the scratch directory while the parent looks up rollouts using the home string without converting it to an absolute path.

findings.verification: Test a clean prefix with a split later enabled record, an alternate tool-list shape, and a filename/metadata ID mismatch on LF and CRLF files. Then run the smoke with a relative home.
findings.remedy: Resolve the home once for parent and children, verify rollout and turn identity, require a complete terminal record and validated recognized evidence, and bound retries for transient reads.

findings.claim: The launch timestamp improves parent-call attribution but does not prevent fast escaped spawns or stale child-rollout stops.
findings.trigger: A turn makes a spawn call then exits before the next poll, or a resumed parent has an older child rollout modified within the five-second slack window.

evidence.observation: An exited child breaks before guard inspection. Child rollout attribution uses a backdated mtime and parent ID rather than a current-turn marker.

findings.verification: Use a fake Codex turn that logs a current spawn and exits before the first poll, then resume a separate thread with a recently modified old child rollout and no current spawn.
findings.remedy: Inspect evidence before accepting normal exit, watch for current spawn events during execution, and bind child attribution to a turn or rollout creation boundary.

findings.claim: Secondary review turns can receive a prompt without the reviewer role constraint while global instructions remain available.
findings.trigger: A timeout continuation, format repair, or same-thread read-insist turn is sent.

evidence.observation: The shared primary assembler adds the sentence. Separate follow-up prompt builders omit it. A fresh read-insist that embeds the original prompt retains it.

findings.verification: Capture stdin or the prompt file for a fake timeout continuation and a same-thread Kimi read-insist turn.
findings.remedy: Use the shared role constraint in every review prompt builder and describe it as an instruction rather than enforced capability isolation.

findings.claim: A detached death record can point at an earlier turn or another consultation, and the terminal stream survives only in memory until the supervisor records death.
findings.trigger: A timeout continuation ends the run, a sibling pending record remains, or the bridge is killed before its terminal status is written.

evidence.observation: The newly noted stream selects a dead read-insist stream or the primary, even when a continuation has its own stream.
Any task pending record can provide the first path before the run's own note. A reader of a dead process receives no note.

findings.verification: Run a detached fake primary timeout followed by a failed continuation while an unrelated pending fixture exists. Check which stream the death record identifies.
findings.remedy: Persist the run ID and current stream on each turn transition and use only matching evidence when constructing its death record.

findings.claim: The providers breakdown measures the presence of a JSON sidecar reference rather than whether a failed run preserved a reply.
findings.trigger: A failed run preserves only a Markdown partial, or its ledger points to a JSON sidecar that has since been removed.

evidence.observation: The counter uses only a nonempty `reply_json` string. Markdown partials are stored separately and raw runs do not create that sidecar.

findings.verification: Preserve a raw timeout partial and inspect the reviewer's `reply_outcomes` in `c3 providers --json`.
findings.remedy: Record the preserved reply kind explicitly and use it for the count, or label the metric as JSON-sidecar presence.
